summary: The note traces early history of the television remote control. Zenith Radio Corporation developed the first remote intended for televisions in 1950, a wired device called "Lazy Bones". In 1955 Eugene Polley developed the Flashmatic, the first wireless TV remote, which used a light beam onto a photoelectric cell but had notable limitations.
one_line: Early history of television remote controls, from Zenith's wired Lazy Bones (1950) to Eugene Polley's light-based Flashmatic (1955).
key_facts: The first remote intended to control a television was developed by Zenith Radio Corporation in 1950.
Zenith's 1950 television remote was called "Lazy Bones".
The Lazy Bones remote was connected to the television by a wire.
A wireless remote control for television, the Flashmatic, was developed in 1955.
Eugene Polley developed the Flashmatic wireless remote control in 1955.
The Flashmatic worked by shining a beam of light onto a photoelectric cell.
The photoelectric cell in the Flashmatic did not distinguish between light from the remote and light from other sources.
The Flashmatic had to be pointed very precisely at the receiver in order to work.
